source_entries.theorem: On connected smooth compact Kähler X, real Kähler class alpha and phi in E1_NA(alpha) with finite integral H_alpha(phi)=integral A_X MA_alpha(phi), there exist actual smooth equivariant relatively Kähler cohomological configurations with data eta_j strongly converging to phi and H_alpha(eta_j) converging to H_alpha(phi).
source_entries.application: Model existence in the partial approximation theorem and joint entropy theorem. Field is C trivially valued; X^beth retains supports; probability mass V^-1; no prescribed extra P-level theorem is assumed.
source_entries.proof_check: Full frozen Section 5 and analytic Rees repair supplied as mathematical data. Reconstructed downstream model entropy and mixed slope applications. Not independently reproving the entire recovery construction.
source_entries.limitation: No historical PASS is used as proof. R does not itself preserve extra P-envelopes.

source_entries.units: Lemma 5.0.5; Theorem 5.2.2; Theorem B; finite-energy supporting inequality in §§2.3,5
source_entries.theorem: For smooth compact Kähler (X,alpha), strong convergence in E1_NA gives energy and supremum convergence and weak convergence of probability MA measures. Weak convergence with bounded J gives integral |phi_j-phi| MA(psi) ->0 for every fixed psi in E1_NA. E(a)-E(b)<=integral(a-b)MA(b).
source_entries.application: Common upper datum energy, B_j ->0, weak measures and discrepancy-tail integrability.
source_entries.proof_check: Primary Lemma 5.0.5 proof and metric-topology proof units read; Calabi–Yau homeomorphism treated as an exact established foundation, not independently reproved.
source_entries.limitation: The constructive Theorem 9.2.1 only produces PL-obstacle envelopes; actual models enter through supplied R.

source_entries.theorem: For compact Kähler X, w in E1(omega) and phi in E1_NA(alpha), the actual maximal weak ray r(w,phi) exists, is order preserving in both arguments, and has affine energy E(w)+t E_alpha(phi) in matched conventions. From zero, sup_X r_t=t sup phi.
source_entries.application: Common upper maximal rays, joint initial-point estimate, energy-defect obstruction, cutoffs.
source_entries.proof_check: Theorem 5.1.7 proof and Lemma 5.3.1 proof read in primary text. Energy-slope proof units read and transport reconstructed in paper.
source_entries.limitation: P-maximal test curves are not assumed maximal for ordinary NA datum; explicit supplied Cantor ray distinguishes them.

source_entries.theorem: Mean-normalized finite-energy mixed-pairing differences have bound C epsilon^q R^(1-q), q=2^-n, where epsilon bounds slot energy distances, R bounds slot J plus fixed supremum-minus-mean constant, and C depends on fixed smooth forms and dimension. Finite-energy decreasing continuity and singular slopes follow by slot replacement.
source_entries.application: Uniform normalized G and fixed-PL-test pairing estimates along eta_j, followed by joint entropy liminf/limsup.
source_entries.proof_check: Complete displayed estimate and singular-approximation proof units read. Paper supplies constants independent of varying eta_j models, mean restoration, sign splitting and calibrated flux.
source_entries.normalization: MP uses i/pi and unsquared time s; use background 2omega, potential r_{2s}, datum 2phi in class 2alpha, then t=2s. Test slopes calibrated by -r F_r/2=F_t.
source_entries.limitation: Only fixed cohomological inputs and one fixed test model in the lower bound. No uniform estimate over all varying SNC test models is asserted.

source_entries.theorem: Discrepancy is a directed supremum of continuous PL model retraction tests. In this paper the discrepancy over X at a Gauss component is (a_i+1-b_i)/b_i and is zero at the trivial valuation.
source_entries.application: Lower-semicontinuous A_X for uniform integrability; after a fixed-model joint liminf take the directed supremum of discrepancy integrals.
source_entries.proof_check: Primary discrepancy/retraction proof unit read. The total-space discrepancy in the source must be shifted by the time weight; paper derives the over-X coefficient from the log-canonical volume.
source_entries.limitation: No arbitrary nonequivariant total-space restriction is silently identified with a valuation over X.

source_entries.units: Theorem 5.5; Corollary 4.14; Theorem 4.17 and energy identities
source_entries.theorem: On E1 of a compact Kähler manifold, canonical weak geodesics have affine normalized energy and constant d1 speed; ordered d1(a,b)=E(a)-E(b) for a>=b; supporting inequality E(a)-E(b)<=integral(a-b)MA(b); I1(a,b)<=C d1(a,b).
source_entries.application: Actual-ray comparison, nonsmooth initial-point transport, mean/slot distances and energy defects.
source_entries.proof_check: Full Theorem 5.5 proof unit read; ordered metric and finite-energy affinity are exact imported foundations, supplied and primary checked for domain.
source_entries.normalization: Source operator i partial barpartial: source potential u/(2pi); energy and d1 multiplied by 2pi/V for probability normalization.

source_entries.units: Darvas–Xia–Zhang, Theorem 2.6; published formula (51), v3 formula (62)
source_entries.theorem: In an arbitrary big class on a smooth compact Kähler manifold, the inverse Legendre transform identifies finite-energy P-maximal test curves and actual weak rays with the prescribed minimal initial potential. The normalized energy slope is lambda^+ + integral_{-infinity}^{lambda^+}(M(lambda)-1) dlambda. General positive-mass relative starts have a separate relative signature.
source_entries.application: Analytic Legendre mass profiles in Kähler background with initial zero; smooth initial w converted to omega_w only.
source_entries.proof_check: Theorem and normalization read in both published and less-garbled v3 primary text. Referenced complete analytic proof units read in DZ and DX.
source_entries.limitation: No algebraic polarization theorem applied to transcendental class; no singular initial background substituted into the minimal-potential formula.

source_entries.theorem: On smooth compact Kähler X in a big real (1,1) class, maximal psh test curves correspond to psh geodesic rays; finite-energy curves correspond to finite-energy rays and satisfy the mass-integral slope formula. Bounded approximants decrease, including their level measures. Interior mass is positive and continuous.
source_entries.application: Complete nonpolarized proof chain for Legendre correspondence and energy formula, actual explicit model ray.
source_entries.proof_check: Entire Theorem 3.7(i),(ii) argument, Proposition 3.8 construction, Theorem 3.9 proof, bounded dyadic energy-sandwich proof Proposition 3.10 read across saved units. Lemma 3.11 refers to DX Lemma 3.9, read separately. Underlying standard pluripotential theorems remain imported.
source_entries.normalization: Printed operator i/(2pi) matches. Minimal potential equals zero in our Kähler background; mass divided by V.

source_entries.units: Darvas–Xia, Theorem 3.7, Proposition 3.8, Lemma 3.9 and associated analytic units in Section 3.1
source_entries.theorem: Bounded P-maximal test curves have actual bounded weak rays and the normalized mass-integral energy formula; interior mass is positive continuous.
source_entries.application: Read analytic Riemann-sum and interior-mass proofs. Nonpolarized applicability independently given by DXZ/DZ.

source_entries.limitation: This paper's global setting is polarized. Its algebraic closure theorems are not applied to our general class.

source_entries.units: Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 3.3; Proposition 2.6
source_entries.theorem: For ordered singularity types [u]<=[v] the singularity pseudometric is the normalized sum of mixed-mass differences 1/((n+1)V) sum_{k=0}^n (integral omega^k <omega_v^(n-k)> - integral omega^k <omega_u^(n-k)>). It has a triangle inequality. Its zero fibers are equal ceilings; at positive mass ceiling equals P-envelope.
source_entries.application: Interior d_S convergence detects finer P-equivalence and is not replaced by multiplier-ideal equivalence.
source_entries.proof_check: Lemma 3.4 and its chordal energy identity read; primary ceiling comparison and positive-mass signature checked.
source_entries.normalization: Printed i partial barpartial potential u/(2pi), probability metric scaled by 2pi/V.

source_entries.theorem: If u<=v are theta-psh on a compact Kähler manifold, raw top mass m(u)>0 and b>1 obeys b^n m(u)>(b^n-1)m(v), then P_theta(bu+(1-b)v) is theta-psh (not identically -infinity).
source_entries.application: For ordered interior levels, choose b=(M_v/(2(M_v-M_u)))^(1/n); convex decomposition gives all mixed-mass differences <=k/b and d_S<= n/(2b). Through common upper level this proves all-dimensional interior convergence.
source_entries.proof_check: Complete Lemma 4.3 contradiction proof and contact-set estimate proof Lemma 4.4, including continuation 1758–1812, read. Lemma 4.5 truncation proof read. Underlying mass monotonicity, plurifine locality and regularization are imported exact foundations.
source_entries.limitation: Only positive mass and strictly interior levels with uniform positive lower bound on compact level intervals; no endpoint conclusion.

source_entries.theorem: Ordered psh singularity types have ordered mixed non-pluripolar masses. A nonpositive psh potential with positive non-pluripolar mass has a model envelope P[u] dominating it, preserving mass and satisfying P[P[u]]=P[u].
source_entries.application: Mass order under common upper levels, mixed convex decomposition, P vs ceiling positive-mass interpretation.
source_entries.proof_check: Mass monotonicity proof-unit excerpts and complete positive-mass envelope proof unit read; standard general non-pluripolar product foundations imported.
source_entries.limitation: No arbitrary zero-mass mass-preservation theorem imported.

source_entries.theorem: A smooth dominating relatively Kähler cohomological test configuration over compact Kähler X has an actual compatible weak ray from any smooth Kähler initial potential, whose divisor-removed total potential has locally bounded complex Hessian.
source_entries.application: Finite-index model entropy slope via determinant domination against a fixed log-canonical fiber volume.
source_entries.proof_check: Complete Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7 proof read; underlying homogeneous Dirichlet regularity theorem is imported, not independently reproved.
source_entries.limitation: Constants may depend on the model index. Printed time-dependent entropy constants not imported.

source_entries.theorem: On compact connected Kähler X, the Chen–Tian Mabuchi functional extends to E1 as the greatest d1-lower-semicontinuous extension and is convex along canonical finite-energy weak geodesics. Smooth contracted energies extend d1 continuously.
source_entries.application: Convex finite-index M_j bounds using recovered slopes and passage at fixed time to the target ray. Joint entropy upper bound after uniform mixed control.
source_entries.proof_check: Complete Theorem 4.7 proof unit read; contracted-energy foundations imported with exact signature.
source_entries.normalization: Operator i partial barpartial converted with u/(2pi). Ricci and average scalar curvature scale by 2pi, canceling energy scaling; full probability entropy coefficient remains one.
source_entries.limitation: No entropy continuity at arbitrary fixed-time d1 limits is asserted.

source_entries.units: Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2; comparison proof consulted for boundary checks
source_entries.theorem: Locally bounded psh functions have symmetric multilinear positive current products, weakly continuous under decreasing locally bounded limits. For locally C1,1 potentials convolution identifies products with almost-everywhere coefficient products.
source_entries.application: Fiber measures, model density domination and explicit piecewise C1,1 ray calculation. Actual-ray identification supplied by direct P-level calculation and Legendre theorem, not an unproved subgeodesic recognition assertion.
source_entries.proof_check: Theorem 2.1 statement and proof units read; convolution identification supplied in paper. Local comparison/uniqueness proofs also consulted but not essential to actual-ray identification.
source_entries.limitation: No mixed products of unbounded psh functions defined by bounded BT alone.

source_entries.theorem: For proper f:X->Y, invertible L and a point y whose fiber restriction L_y is ample, an open neighborhood V of y exists on which L is relatively ample.
source_entries.application: The explicit rational blowup bundle has positive degrees c and1-c on nodal central components and degree1 elsewhere; after a denominator, direct component sections prove fiber ampleness and the proper-morphism theorem proves relative ampleness.
source_entries.proof_check: Complete primary statement and proof read.
source_entries.limitation: Actual explicit algebraic curve configuration only; general transcendental models supplied by R.
